item.title: College can be a big life change. How can students navigate mental health challenges?
item.description: A study published this week in the Journal of American College Health found that more than half of U.S. college students report feeling lonely.

item.title: Epstein survivor on former Prince Andrew's arrest
item.description: The former prince was previously stripped of his royal titles over his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Endangered squirrel clings to life high atop Arizona mountain
item.description: Mt. Graham is known as a sky island, a mountain ecosystem surrounded by a “sea of desert.”

item.title: Winter Olympics day 13: The latest
item.description: It is a big day on the ice with medal events in speed skating and women’s figure skating. Plus, Team USA is taking on Team Canada in the women's Olympic hockey gold medal game.

item.title: A messy mix of rain and snow expected Friday
item.description: The weather the next few days brings a little bit of everything: snow, sleet, freezing rain and rain. What you get depends on where you are — and just as importantly, what time of day it is. Meanwhile, the storm potential for Sunday is still up in the air.

item.title: Healey housing secretary stepping down to take banking job
item.description: Ed Augustus is the eighth cabinet secretary to leave during Healey's term. He is set to become CEO of UniBank. Replacing him as housing secretary is Rep. Juana Matias, a Democrat who represented Lawrence in the House.

item.title: How to change a memory
item.description: Neuroscientist Steve Ramirez sees memory as a way to time travel. But what if we could edit our memories?

item.title: Working group recommends more police and a new 'recovery' court for 'Mass. and Cass'
item.description: The working group says their recommendations will address drug use and homelessness in the neighborhood. But some are concerned the proposed steps signal an increasingly punitive approach and that there are not adequate resources to implement them.

item.title: MIT cut ties with diversity nonprofit following federal inquiry
item.description: MIT has cut ties with a national nonprofit focused on diversifying university faculties following pressure from the Trump administration.

item.title: Healey won't attend White House events with governors
item.description: Gov. Maura Healey won't attend a White House meeting Friday and dinner on Saturday with other governors, saying President Trump’s politicized the event.
